evidence.title: ‘Another coup d’état’: fears grow as Flávio Bolsonaro vows to ‘re-democratise’ Brazil

occurrences.checkable_against: V-Dem liberal democracy index
occurrences.quote_span: Bolsonaro did not spell out what he meant by “re-democratising” Brazil, a vibrant if polarised multiparty democracy that the Sweden-based V-Dem institute ranks 28th on its liberal democracy index, two places ahead of the UK and 23 ahead of the US.
occurrences.speaker: V-Dem institute
occurrences.subject: Flávio Bolsonaro's Brazil presidential campaign

occurrences.checkable_against: Historical records and statements from the 1964 Brazilian coup
occurrences.quote_span: Danilo Araújo Marques, a historian, said the word “democracy” had been co-opted before in Brazil by undemocratic forces, when the military men and politicians behind the 1964 coup called their actions “an intervention to democratise the country”.
occurrences.speaker: Danilo Araújo Marques
occurrences.subject: Flávio Bolsonaro's Brazil presidential campaign

occurrences.checkable_against: Brazilian presidential appointment and prison-release records
occurrences.quote_span: Jair Bolsonaro and his jailed co-conspirators are likely to be freed if his son wins, with the former president expected to become an influential minister able to select the new heads of the armed forces.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: Flávio Bolsonaro's Brazil presidential campaign

occurrences.checkable_against: Celso Rocha de Barros's interview or published statement
occurrences.quote_span: Celso Rocha de Barros, a political scientist, said he believed that by using the word “re-democratise”, Flávio Bolsonaro sought “to smuggle his authoritarian purposes into acceptable language”.
occurrences.speaker: Celso Rocha de Barros
occurrences.subject: Flávio Bolsonaro's Brazil presidential campaign

occurrences.checkable_against: Flávio Bolsonaro campaign remarks about Lula and the future
occurrences.quote_span: Marques noted that during the campaign, Bolsonaro had claimed his octogenarian opponent, Lula, represented the past while he was selling the future.
occurrences.speaker: Danilo Araújo Marques
occurrences.subject: Flávio Bolsonaro's Brazil presidential campaign

occurrences.checkable_against: El Salvador constitutional amendments and presidential election rules
occurrences.quote_span: Nayib Bukele, El Salvador’s authoritarian president, has been accused of “killing” democracy by using control over the country’s congress and institutions to approve sweeping constitutional changes, including scrapping presidential term limits so he can seek indefinite re-election.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: Flávio Bolsonaro's Brazil presidential campaign

occurrences.checkable_against: Marcelo Freixo's public statement and Brazil historical records
occurrences.quote_span: Marcelo Freixo, a newly elected congressman from Lula’s Workers’ party (PT), said: “Brazil was re-democratised in 1988. The person who tried to undo this was his father, who was convicted of an attempted coup. What they want, once again, is a coup.”
occurrences.speaker: Marcelo Freixo
occurrences.subject: Flávio Bolsonaro's Brazil presidential campaign

occurrences.checkable_against: Flávio Bolsonaro campaign event recording or transcript in Goiânia
occurrences.quote_span: “The only thing standing in the way of Brazil becoming a barbarity is called Flávio Bolsonaro as president,” he claimed at a campaign event in Goiânia, a city near the capital, Brasília.
occurrences.speaker: Flávio Bolsonaro
occurrences.subject: Flávio Bolsonaro's Brazil presidential campaign

occurrences.checkable_against: Brazil historical records on the military dictatorship and democratic transition
occurrences.quote_span: Brazil was re-democratised in the 1980s after a brutal 21-year dictatorship that Flávio’s father, the disgraced ex-president Jair Bolsonaro, has long praised.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: Flávio Bolsonaro's Brazil presidential campaign

occurrences.checkable_against: Flávio Bolsonaro campaign speech or video from 2026-10-06
occurrences.quote_span: On Tuesday, the rightwinger vowed to capitalise on the hugely increased far-right presence in congress after the election to change the constitution and “re-democratise this country”.
occurrences.speaker: Flávio Bolsonaro
occurrences.subject: Flávio Bolsonaro's Brazil presidential campaign

occurrences.checkable_against: Míriam Leitão's O Globo column
occurrences.quote_span: Writing in O Globo newspaper, Míriam Leitão, a prominent political and economic journalist, warned that if Bolsonaro won, Brazil faced “the extreme and concrete danger of … another coup d’état attempt”.
occurrences.speaker: Míriam Leitão
occurrences.subject: Flávio Bolsonaro's Brazil presidential campaign

occurrences.checkable_against: Talíria Petrone's X post
occurrences.quote_span: Talíria Petrone, the leftwing congresswoman, wrote on X: “This is the announcement of a coup.”
occurrences.speaker: Talíria Petrone
occurrences.subject: Flávio Bolsonaro's Brazil presidential campaign

occurrences.checkable_against: Flávio Bolsonaro press remarks or transcript about his meeting with Gustavo Villatoro
occurrences.quote_span: Bolsonaro told reporters that during their conversation, Villatoro “stressed the importance” of using control of congress to make the “necessary legal changes”.
occurrences.speaker: Flávio Bolsonaro
occurrences.subject: Flávio Bolsonaro's Brazil presidential campaign

occurrences.checkable_against: Miguel Lago interview and Brazil Senate election results
occurrences.quote_span: Miguel Lago, a political scientist, said Sunday’s far-right election triumph – in which Bolsonaro’s Liberal party (PL) secured the senate’s largest caucus, with 28 of its 81 seats – would permit radical changes, including the impeachment of supreme court ministers considered enemies of the Bolsonarismo movement.
occurrences.speaker: Miguel Lago
occurrences.subject: Flávio Bolsonaro's Brazil presidential campaign
